title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
desc: The sparkling comedy of manners that made Jane Austen immortal — Elizabeth Bennet meets the proud Mr Darcy, and neither of them is prepared for what follows.

author: George Orwell
desc: Winston Smith rewrites the past for a government that controls every thought. Orwell's masterpiece remains the definitive novel of surveillance and truth.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
desc: Jazz-age New York, a mysterious millionaire, and a green light across the bay — the great American novel of longing and reinvention.

title: Where the Crawdads Sing
author: Delia Owens
desc: A murder mystery, a coming-of-age story and a love letter to the marshes of North Carolina — the phenomenon that sold over 15 million copies.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
desc: Through the eyes of Scout Finch, Harper Lee's masterpiece explores race, justice and conscience in the American South — as urgent today as the day it was published.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
desc: Holden Caulfield, a disaffected teenager in 1950s New York, in the novel that changed how a generation talked about growing up.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
desc: The Buendía family and the town of Macondo, in the century-spanning novel that put magical realism on the world's bookshelves.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
desc: Connell and Marianne's love story unfolds across years and distances in Sally Rooney's razor-sharp portrait of intimacy and class.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
desc: The bestselling science fiction novel of all time — Paul Atreides, the desert planet Arrakis, and the spice that shapes the galaxy.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
desc: Bilbo Baggins, a dragon, a ring and an adventure that changed fantasy forever. The book that started Middle-earth.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
desc: Kvothe recounts the story of his life — from a trouper's wagon to the University — in a debut fantasy that became an instant classic.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
desc: Case, a washed-up console cowboy, is offered one last job in the Sprawl. The novel that invented cyberpunk and won the Hugo, Nebula and Philip K. Dick awards.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
desc: An envoy arrives on Gethen, a world where gender is fluid and winter never ends. Le Guin's Hugo- and Nebula-winning meditation on identity and trust.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
desc: Ryland Grace wakes up alone on a spaceship with no memory of his mission — and the fate of two worlds in his hands. A joyride of a science thriller.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
desc: A snowbound train, a murdered passenger, and thirteen suspects. Hercule Poirot faces his most famous case.

title: The Da Vinci Code
author: Dan Brown
desc: Robert Langdon races through Paris and London decoding a mystery hidden in Leonardo's masterpieces. The thriller that defined a decade.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
desc: A disgraced journalist and a brilliant hacker investigate a forty-year-old disappearance in Larsson's electrifying Millennium trilogy opener.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
desc: On their fifth wedding anniversary, Amy Dunne disappears. Her husband Nick is the prime suspect — and nothing is what it seems. The twistiest thriller of its era.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
desc: Alicia Berenson hasn't spoken a word since she shot her husband. A forensic psychotherapist is determined to make her talk — and uncover the truth.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
desc: How did an unremarkable ape become the ruler of the planet? Harari's sweeping history of humankind is essential, brilliant reading.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
desc: From the Big Bang to black holes — Stephen Hawking's landmark tour of the universe, written for everyone.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
desc: A Nobel laureate explains the two systems that drive how we think — and why we are so often wrong. The modern classic of behavioural science.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
desc: Tiny changes, remarkable results. James Clear's practical, evidence-based system for building good habits and breaking bad ones — one per cent at a time.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank
desc: The extraordinary diary of a girl in hiding during the Second World War — one of the most widely read books in the world.

title: Long Walk to Freedom
author: Nelson Mandela
desc: The autobiography of Nelson Mandela — from a village childhood to twenty-seven years in prison to the presidency of a new South Africa.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
desc: Born to survivalists in the mountains of Idaho, Tara Westover didn't set foot in a classroom until seventeen — then walked into Cambridge. A memoir of self-invention.

title: The Waste Land and Other Poems
author: T.S. Eliot
desc: The most influential poem of the twentieth century, together with 'The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock' and other landmarks of modernist verse.

title: Milk and Honey
author: Rupi Kaur
desc: Rupi Kaur's debut collection — the hurting, the loving, the breaking, the healing — read by millions and translated into more than forty languages.

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
author: Eric Carle
desc: The beloved classic that has eaten its way into the hearts of millions — a tiny caterpillar with a very big appetite.

title: Matilda
author: Roald Dahl
desc: Matilda Wormwood is a genius, her parents don't care, and Miss Trunchbull is a terror — until Matilda discovers she can do something remarkable.

title: Charlotte's Web
author: E.B. White
desc: Wilbur the pig is saved by a spider who spins words into her web. E.B. White's tender masterpiece about friendship and saying goodbye.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
desc: Ten strangers, an island, and a nursery rhyme counting them down. The best-selling mystery novel of all time — Christie's masterpiece of suspense.

title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
author: Roald Dahl
desc: Charlie Bucket wins a golden ticket to Willy Wonka's extraordinary factory — where the chocolate flows and the Oompa-Loompas sing.
